rationale: The answer is a thorough, evidence-backed architecture review. I independently verified every load-bearing factual claim: the Electron desktop classification; the three coexisting IPC mechanisms (typed handlers in src/main/ipc, inline ipcMain.on/handle in App/WindowManager, and the ipcMain.emit internal bus); the sender-derived vs windowId identity split with the duplicate window-add-file-path channel pair; the restoreBufferId type-assertion on BrowserWindow; the dual command systems; the 2-window WindowType model; the @muyajs/core engine boundary with dead muya alias and legacy @marktext/muyajs dependency; BUFFERED_STATE_VERSION=1; the absence of an ADR directory; and the three documentation-drift findings (CLAUDE.md architecture section vs config.ts, plus ARCHITECTURE.md/TYPESCRIPT.md pre-monorepo layout) — all confirmed against source. Documentation drift is flagged, classified, and not relied upon as current, so it does not block the gate. The one factual error is a minor count overstatement (~30 vs actual 20 ipcMain.emit in file.ts) that does not change the recommendation. Options include status quo, a recommended consolidation (B), and a rejected speculative abstraction (C), each with trade-offs, assumptions, and invalidation conditions; migration steps are incremental, grep/typecheck-observable, and revertible, with concrete exit criteria. All nine dimensions merit full credit; the review is decision-ready at 18/18 with the accuracy gate passing.
